say.en: The firm has sold everything and has a pile of cash. Creditors, a partner who lent money, and all the partners want their share. The law fixes the queue. Section 48 gives that order. In this lesson: State the order of payment under Section 48.
Explain the treatment of firm's debts and private debts Section 49.

body.en: Losses, including deficiency of capital, are paid first out of profits, then out of capital, and lastly by partners individually in their profit sharing ratio. The assets, including sums contributed by partners, are applied in this *order*: (i) debts of the firm to third parties; (ii) advances (loans) by partners, ratably; (iii) capital of each partner, ratably; (iv) any surplus is divided among partners in the profit sharing ratio.
body.kn: ನಷ್ಟಗಳನ್ನು ಮೊದಲು ಲಾಭದಿಂದ, ನಂತರ ಬಂಡವಾಳದಿಂದ, ಕೊನೆಗೆ ಪಾಲುದಾರರು ಲಾಭ ಹಂಚಿಕೆ ಅನುಪಾತದಲ್ಲಿ ಭರಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಆಸ್ತಿಗಳ ಹಣವನ್ನು ಕ್ರಮವಾಗಿ: ಹೊರಗಿನ ಸಾಲಗಾರರು, ಪಾಲುದಾರರ ಸಾಲ, ಪಾಲುದಾರರ ಬಂಡವಾಳ, ಉಳಿದದ್ದು ಲಾಭ ಹಂಚಿಕೆ ಅನುಪಾತದಲ್ಲಿ.

say.en: Let us work this out together, step by step. On dissolution, cash available after realising all assets is 1,80,000 rupees. Creditors 80,000 rupees; A's loan to the firm 20,000 rupees; capitals A 30,000 rupees and B 30,000 rupees; profit sharing ratio 1:1. Show the order of payment.
Pay outside creditors 80,000 rupees gives 1,00,000 rupees left.
Repay A's loan 20,000 rupees gives 80,000 rupees left.
Repay capitals A 30,000 rupees and B 30,000 rupees gives 20,000 rupees left.
Surplus 20,000 rupees shared 1:1 gives A 10,000, rupees B 10,000 rupees.
So the answer is A receives 20,000 rupees plus 30,000 rupees plus 10,000 rupees equals 60,000 rupees; B receives 40,000 rupees.
